newsitem.title: UK: London gold lags as precious metals advance.
newsitem.headline: London gold lags as precious metals advance.

text.p: Precious metals prices were sharply firmer on Friday morning with the exception of gold which continued a drift of the past two weeks.

Silver added to its gains from Thursday and platinum and palladium were both stronger on a strike threat from South Africa's Impala Platinum refinery, panic short covering on Tokyo Tocom futures and continued tight supply in Europe.
Zurich was closed for Switzerland's National Day holiday.
Gold was fixed at $325.30 per ounce down $1.05 from Thursday afternoon's close and reflecting a lower close on New York Comex futures and a weaker tone in Asia.
"There is some good physical demand for gold and silver but it is not exceptional," one dealer said.
"The high dollar in Germany for instance is making gold more expensive now than it was at the beginning of the year," the dealer added.

Dealers said gold could weaken today and there was the prospect of a return to levels around $320.00 last seen in mid July after several attempts failed in the past 10 days to get through the $328-$330.00 resistance.
The outlook for silver was much brighter after the Comex locals finally shepherded it through $4.40 resistance, triggered buy stops and won fund support.
It was six cents firmer at $4.48/$4.50 with the prospect of another charge to come.
"There is a gap on the charts at $4.50-$4.55 and if they decide to fill that, then that could help silver to target $4.80-$4.90," one dealer said.
The strong dollar brought further short covering from the Tocom investors who ensured that palladium futures went limit up for the third day in succession.
Palladium fixed at $227.00, its highest since June 9, 1997.
Dealers said Russian delayed deliveries of palladium were beginning to arrive at European merchants but they were in small quantities and palladium remained tight and in backwardation.
"Deliveries have started from Russia to Europe. The tightness is largely in palladium as there is enough platinum to satisfy most demand in Europe," a dealer said.
Impala's refinery workers ignored their union's strike call on Friday morning, according to the company.
Platinum was indicated at $435.00/$438.00 up $8.50 and palladium at $224.00/$227.00 a gain of $$1 .80.
